A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DFS and product-of-experts approach to ARC. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and matchable despite the revised title and appendix organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original ARC accuracy, runtime and ablation results, plus a preliminary Sudoku experiment in Appendix A.1.

after.justification: V2 retains the original ARC experiments and reports ConceptARC and Sudoku 3M evaluations in Sections 5.5–5.6.

M1.justification: Augmented training, thresholded DFS generation and product-of-experts ranking remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Expanded descriptions clarify existing operations; the revised Sudoku setup changes experimental settings rather than the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 evaluates ConceptARC's concept-organized tasks, which v1 only discusses, and replaces procedurally generated Sudoku puzzles with 50% missing cells with sampled Sudoku 3M puzzles. This substantially broadens and revises evaluation coverage while retaining ARC-AGI and RE-ARC.

E2.justification: ARC comparator sets remain unchanged. The revised Sudoku comparison adds mean-probability selection in Figure 6, whereas v1 Appendix A.1 reports only maximum-probability selection versus PoE. The cited results from Seely et al. are contextual comparisons, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The Sudoku evaluation is substantially redesigned: v1 uses 2,000 training puzzles and 400 test puzzles; v2 fine-tunes an ARC-pretrained Llama 3B on 128,000 Sudoku tasks and tests 1,000 unseen puzzles, explicitly specifying top-1 accuracy and DFS T=1%. Both omit Sudoku test-time training. Existing ARC settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a Sudoku threshold-sensitivity analysis comparing candidate coverage, overall accuracy and conditional selection accuracy across ranking strategies. V1 reports only a single preliminary Sudoku comparison. The existing ARC component ablations, search comparisons and ranking analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental error bars. The probability thresholds and selection-confidence curves concern model predictions, not statistical uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: ARC Tables 1–3 retain their results, including 71.6% accuracy. V2 adds 73.3% ConceptARC accuracy and replaces v1's preliminary Sudoku results of 70.5% baseline and 97.5% PoE with 53% top-1 accuracy on Sudoku 3M and 100% selection accuracy conditional on generating the correct solution. These Sudoku scores use different settings and do not establish a performance decline.

T1.justification: The probability definitions, augmentation assumptions and Theorem 4.1 remain unchanged. The full appendix theorem and proof are preserved, with Appendix A renumbered as Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and concluding discussion retain the same central claims: dual use of one LLM for generation and scoring, 71.6% ARC accuracy, low inference cost and potential generalization through valid transformations. The expanded title foregrounds an existing contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds concrete explanations of autoregressive error propagation and DFS's memory and runtime advantages. It also interprets ConceptARC performance as evidence against overfitting and attributes perfect conditional Sudoku selection to easier correctness checking. New future-work discussion specifies possible extensions beyond grid puzzles.

D1.justification: V1's promised release becomes a stated public model/code release with a GitHub link. V2 clarifies augmentation randomization and negative-log thresholds while retaining the ARC training and token tables. The replacement Sudoku study documents its model and data source but does not specify an epoch count, unlike v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds Radcliffe's Sudoku dataset and Seely et al.'s Sudoku evaluation work, introducing additional Sudoku research positioning. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate entries; the main ARC positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands the title, makes localized explanatory rewrites, adds ConceptARC, Sudoku and Future Work subsections, and labels the appendix sections for the algorithm, parameters and proof. Author affiliations and publication information also change. The overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Sudoku Figure 6, expands Figure 4 and Table 2 captions, and adjusts figure sizing and appendix layout. Algorithm commentary is separated from its display, and appendix tables are repositioned. Existing ARC plots and table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: ConceptARC testing and the revised Sudoku evaluation broaden empirical support, while the threshold analysis, clearer explanations and documented model/code access improve usability. These are useful but limited gains around unchanged ARC results and theory. The Sudoku studies are not directly comparable, and v2's comparison with other LLMs relies on cited results from different benchmarks rather than matched evaluations.
